transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-07
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Oliver Grant (Verdance CTO); Sana Iqbal (ML Lead); Marcus Lee (Infra); Priya Desai (Product)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20261107-8237 (internal)

Auto-summary (auto):
Verdance wants to evaluate open model choices for large-context, multilingual retail search/ranking and a tool-calling path for inventory/price lookup. Main constraints: P95 latency target 250-300ms for user-facing intents, batch/async for heavy rerank, strict PCI-adjacent data handling, and SSO+audit logs. Considering hosted to start, but strong interest in Dedicated or Private VPC for data residency and auditability. Next steps: pricing TCO, benchmark run, security docs.

Topics:
- Open model comparison (Llama2/3-family, Mistral, local distilled variants)
- Context length: up to 70k tokens for session-level history and catalog context
- Multilingual support (en/es/pt/fr; occasional zh)
- Tool-calling: inventory api, price check, user account lookup
- Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
- Cost/latency tradeoffs; quantization and batching

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: morning everyone, thanks for carving out time, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll hand it to Maya for the deep bits in a bit but quick intros?
[00:07] Oliver: hey Jordan, Oliver here, CTO at Verdance — we run retail search and personalization, really excited to understand the model and deploy tradeoffs.
[00:12] Sana: Sana, ML lead, running prod ranking models today, we have a messy stack with embeddings from two vendors.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus, infra, i'll be doing the VPC stuff if we go private.
[00:21] Jordan: great, thanks. Maya?
[00:23] Maya: yeah hi all, Maya Chen, solutions engineer — i'll cover latency profiles, batching, kv cache, and what dedicated/private buys you.
[00:30] Priya: Priya, product — mainly watching for cost per engagement and rollout cadence.

[00:45] Jordan: quick framing — Verdance told us you're looking at big contexts, multilingual, and some tool-calling. wanted to confirm success criteria. Oliver, maybe you lead?
[00:52] Oliver: sure, main things: 1) user-facing autocomplete/assist needs P95 under 300ms; 2) rerank pipeline can be async but needs throughput; 3) we need multilingual parity across English, Spanish, Portuguese and French — occasional Chinese; 4) data can't leave region for EU customers; 5) we need strong audit logs and SSO.
[01:15] Maya: awesome, that maps well to Redwood's hosted/dedicated/private options — hosted gives fastest time to value, dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and data isolation, private is VPC/on-prem for residency.

[01:35] Sana: first question — for a 70k context window (we have session + catalog + conversation), which open models do we look at, and what are realistic latency profiles?
[01:45] Maya: good question. For 70k you basically need models that support long-context architectures — there are open checkpoints we can run with Redwood's runtime. Realistically, smaller Llama-family weights with rotary/ALiBi optimizations or specialized long-context variants like LongLlama/extended context Mistral variants. Latency depends a lot on seq length for attention cost, kernel choices, and KV cache behavior.
[02:10] Jordan: to give numbers — on Dedicated with A100/RTX-class GPUs and optimized kernels we see tail latencies for medium-size long-context generative requests in the 180-450ms ballpark depending on token generation length; hosted clusters are similar but multi-tenant routing can add small variance — dedicated reduces that variance.
[02:34] Marcus: ok session — we can't take EU data out of region for regulatory reasons. Is Redwood Private required or Dedicated in an EU region enough?
[02:42] Maya: Dedicated in an EU region with customer data isolation meets most needs; Private is for VPC/on-prem where you want the control plane private. Both support KMS integration, audit logs, and RBAC.
[02:56] Marcus: and SSO?
[02:58] Jordan: SSO/SAML supported, plus fine-grained RBAC in Console. we'll send snippet of our compliance pack.

[03:12] Sana: multilingual — we need parity quality for en/es/pt/fr, any models you recommend that don't tank in es/pt?
[03:20] Maya: Mistral newer family plus some of the larger Llama3 models tend to be strong in roman-latin languages; also you can run multilingual fine-tuning or adapter layers. For cost we often recommend a dual-path: smaller distilled for EN + EU-latin fast path and a larger high-capacity model for fallback or hallucination-prone cases.
[03:48] Oliver: hmm fallback path — do you have built-in routing to model variants? we'd like to route by latency budget and by user locale.
[03:56] Jordan: yes, smart routing is first class — you can route by policy (latency, cost, region) and Redwood can fall back to a compatible variant automatically.

[04:10] Sana: tool-calling — inventory API and price check are critical. we need structured responses with tool calls that do not leak PII. how do you separate tool data and model logs?
[04:22] Maya: tool-calling is supported; the runtime can redact or not store tool payloads depending on your retention policy. Audit logs record that a tool call happened, but payloads can be excluded at ingestion. KMS and HSM options for keys.
[04:40] Marcus: what about KV cache persistence — we want session cache across short lived requests to avoid recomputing prefix encodings.
[04:48] Maya: Redwood supports KV cache in-memory with optional persisted caches for warm-starts. For private deployments you can tune cache lifetime. That is important for 70k contexts to avoid re-encoding catalog context every single request.

[05:05] [Jordan, slightly off mic] Jordan: sorry — background noise.
[05:12] Oliver: no worries. so pricing ballpark — do you have guidance for hosted vs dedicated costs for our expected traffic? we estimate 3 million user queries/mo and peak 200 qps during sales.
[05:25] Jordan: we'll share a TCO spreadsheet but rough guidance: hosted pays per-token; for heavy steady usage Dedicated reserved capacity with autoscaling gives better unit economics. Also quantization reduces GPU memory and cost. For 70k context you may need high-memory GPUs or sharded runtime which affects price.
[05:47] Sana: quantization concern — we've seen quality regression with aggressive 4-bit quant. how does Redwood handle quant tradeoffs?
[05:55] Maya: Redwood Optimize gives model + quantization recommendations per workload; there are quant-aware evals. We can run your prompt set to show quality delta vs latency/cost — often a mixed strategy works (quantized for majority fast paths, unquantized for high-fidelity or fallback calls).
[06:18] Priya: any caveats on streaming vs non-streaming for latency? our UI favors streaming for feel.
[06:25] Maya: streaming is supported; for long-context generation streaming can slightly change tail latency but improves perceived latency.
[06:33] Marcus: security follow-ups — we need SOC2, ISO docs, and ability to ingest logs into our SIEM.
[06:39] Jordan: yes, we'll send SOC2 excerpt; we support pushing audit logs to customer endpoints or S3, and offer integrations with common SIEMs.

[07:00] Sana: can we do a quick scenario — user asks a price check which requires tool call, then the assistant should call inventory service and then surface results in Spanish. walk us through how you'd set this up?
[07:12] Maya: sure. step one: define tool definition in Redwood Console with a secure webhook to your inventory microservice; second: mark tool payloads as non-persistent if you don't want them logged; third: set model routing policy to prefer the fast multilingual variant for simple queries and the higher-capacity for fallbacks. We'll show an example wiring with function-like tool calls and a JSON schema for the API to keep responses structured.
[07:43] Sana: and you'd translate via the model or pass to a separate translation tool? we prefer model-native when possible.
[07:49] Maya: model-native translation is fine for en/es/pt/fr for many models; for critical phrasing we run translation engines or specialized translation tool-calls.

[08:05] Oliver: about rollback and canarying — we want canary 10% traffic for new model or quant profiles. does Console support automatic fallback?
[08:15] Jordan: yes, rollouts include canary and A/B and automatic fallback policies if latency or error rates climb. We'll demo the console but i'll also include screenshots in the follow-up.

[08:30] [Timestamp jumps as conversation covers examples; transcript imperfect] 
[08:30] Marcus: ok for private deployment — network diagram? we need to know what agents talk to our VPC.
[08:36] Maya: we typically show a reference architecture — control plane endpoints for the customer-managed control plane, service endpoints inside the VPC, optional on-prem edge for air-gapped. We'll attach the VPC playbook.
[08:48] Oliver: do you support hardware commitments — we want guaranteed throughput for peak season.
[08:52] Jordan: Dedicated reserved capacity contracts cover guaranteed throughput with SLA; we also offer burst policies.

[09:05] Sana: evaluation plan idea — we want: 1) run our 3 prompt sets, 2) run multilingual quality eval, 3) perf bench at peak QPS with 70k contexts and tool-calling integrated. can Redwood help orchestrate these?
[09:18] Maya: yes, we can run the bench in hosted sandbox or on a dedicated pool. We'll need sample dataset and expected SLAs; Maya: we'll also instrument KV cache and show hit/miss metrics so you can see cost breakouts.
[09:33] Oliver: about tokenization — some of our catalog data has HTML and structured fields; how do you recommend constructing the context?
[09:40] Maya: mix of structured fields and HTML-cleaned text; we recommend vector-embedding for product metadata and prefixing dynamic user signals. For very large catalog slices we recommend storing in a retrieval layer and only injecting top-k retrieved chunks into the 70k window, with KV caching for catalog embeddings.
[09:58] Sana: are there limits for model calling throughput with tool-calls? we worry about synchronous blocking on external inventory services.
[10:05] Maya: you can pattern async tool-calls where the model emits a tool instruction which your service picks up; Redwood supports sync and async patterns, plus retry/backoff and circuit breakers at the runtime.
[10:20] Marcus: latency again — if we do 200 qps peak with 70k contexts, any rough CPU/GPU needs?
[10:28] Maya: rough sketch: depends on generation length; for short responses (~20 tokens) throughput is mostly limited by token-generation rates — with sharded high-memory GPUs you can hit 100s of RPS for small outputs; for large context encoding cost grows — that's where KV cache reduces the per-request cost. We'll produce a sizing guide tailored to your prompt sets.
[10:47] Oliver: competitors — we've been talking to Anthropic and Bedrock; what pitfalls should we watch for?
[10:53] Jordan: Anthropic's models are strong but may have less flexible private deployment options depending on partner; Bedrock ties you into the cloud provider. Redwood's differentiator is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with rollout controls and cost tooling.
[11:09] Priya: for ROI calculations, can you show real numbers on token costs vs dedicated reserved?
[11:14] Jordan: yes, TCO spreadsheet — we'll attach example math with your traffic profile.
[11:20] Sana: on hallucination mitigation — we need rerank with grounding; is Redwood supporting retrieval-augmented generation and rerank pipelines?
[11:28] Maya: absolutely. Redwood supports RAG, integrated retrieval connectors, and reranking endpoints. You can run rerank as batch jobs for heavy traffic.
[11:37] Oliver: one more — how do you manage model versioning and rollout audit for compliance teams?
[11:44] Maya: Console logs model versions, rollout history, who triggered deployments, and you can export audit trails. We also keep token-level cost and latency breakdown per model.
[11:54] Jordan: ok let's recap and next milestones — i'll send pricing and SOC2 and an invite for the perf deep-dive with Marcus and Maya. Maya will run the first benchmark and we'll need Verdance prompt sets. Oliver, can you confirm the dataset share?
[12:05] Oliver: yes we'll drop a sanitized subset to the shared s3 bucket and i'll include compliance constraints.
[12:12] Priya: timeline — we'd like a pilot before Black Friday (late Nov), so target quick turnaround.
[12:18] Jordan: noted, we'll prioritize the benchmark.
[12:22] Sana: thanks all.
[12:25] Jordan: thanks everyone. End of call.
